body:
If you’re asking how to get your Florida real estate license in Daytona Beach Shores, here’s the short version: there’s no separate Daytona Beach Shores exam or local license to chase. Every agent in Florida, whether they end up working this stretch of barrier island, the mainland, or anywhere else in the state, earns the same statewide credential, the Florida real estate sales associate license. Daytona Beach Shores is a small, dense coastal town of about 5,200 people, sandwiched between Daytona Beach and Ponce Inlet, but its candidates go through the exact same six-step process as anyone else in Volusia County. Here’s exactly what it involves, step by step.

The 6-step licensing process

The Florida Department of Business and Professional Regulation (DBPR) oversees a fixed process for every applicant in the state:

  1. Meet the basic requirements. Be at least 18 years old with a high school diploma or equivalent and a U.S. Social Security number.
  2. Complete the 63-hour pre-license course. This state-approved course, taken online or in a classroom, ends with a school final exam you must pass before moving forward.
  3. Get fingerprinted. Florida requires electronic fingerprinting through a state-approved vendor so it can run your background check. Do this early, since results must be on file before your application is reviewed.
  4. Apply to the DBPR. Submit your license application online. Once your course completion, fingerprints, and application are all approved, the state issues an exam authorization.
  5. Pass the state exam. The exam is 100 multiple-choice questions, and you need a score of 75% or higher. It’s administered by Pearson VUE, so Daytona Beach Shores candidates simply test at a Pearson VUE testing center near them; there’s no dedicated local test site on this small barrier island.
  6. Activate your license under a broker. Your license stays inactive until a licensed broker activates it, which makes this the biggest real decision in the whole process.

Where do you take the exam?

Pearson VUE administers the Florida sales associate exam at testing centers across the state, and in many cases through online remote proctoring from home. There’s no dedicated Daytona Beach Shores testing site to look for; you simply schedule a slot at a Pearson VUE center near you, most likely in Daytona Beach, once the DBPR issues your exam authorization. Bring valid identification, arrive early, and expect strict security, no phones, no notes, nothing beyond what Pearson VUE allows in the room.

How long does it actually take?

For most Daytona Beach Shores candidates, the process from enrolling in the course to activating a license runs two to four months. The course is the piece you control directly: move through it quickly and everything after tends to follow fast. Fingerprinting, DBPR review, and scheduling the exam each add a bit of processing time on top, regardless of where in Florida you’re starting from.

What does it cost?

Costs vary by course provider and by the state’s current fee schedule, both of which change, so this guide won’t guess at a total. Plan on separate line items for the 63-hour course, fingerprinting, the DBPR application, and the state exam fee. Confirm the current numbers directly with the Florida DBPR before you budget for the process.

After you’re licensed: don’t forget post-license education

Passing the exam isn’t the finish line. Florida requires every sales associate to complete a 45-hour post-license course before their first renewal, which falls between 18 and 24 months after you’re licensed. Miss that deadline and your license can go inactive, even if you’ve been working the whole time. Daytona Beach Shores agents track this the same way every Florida agent does; the calendar doesn’t care how small your town is. A good brokerage keeps you on top of it so it never becomes a surprise.

Why the broker you choose in Daytona Beach Shores matters

Because your license can’t go active without a broker, the brokerage you pick is the first real decision of your career, not a formality at the end. Adams, Cameron & Co. has been Volusia County’s largest brokerage since 1963, headquartered at 600 S. Atlantic Ave in Daytona Beach, just up the coast from Daytona Beach Shores. New agents activating with Adams, Cameron & Co. get in-house marketing and technology at no cost, non-competing managers with access seven days a week, and mentorship built for people brand new to the business, so the license you just earned actually turns into a working career.

The steps above cover the licensing mechanics. For the fuller picture, what the Daytona Beach Shores market looks like for a new agent and what to expect once you’re working, see our guide to becoming an agent in Daytona Beach Shores. Requirements and fees are set by the State of Florida and can change. Always confirm current specifics with the Florida DBPR before you apply. This guide is educational and isn’t legal advice.

faq.q: How many hours of pre-license education do I need in Daytona Beach Shores?
faq.a: The same as anywhere in Florida: a 63-hour state-approved sales associate pre-license course, taken online or in a classroom, with a passing score on the school's final exam.

faq.q: What score do I need to pass the Florida real estate exam?
faq.a: You need 75% or higher on the 100-question state exam, administered by Pearson VUE. Daytona Beach Shores candidates test at a Pearson VUE testing center near them, not a special local site.

faq.q: How much does it cost to get licensed in Daytona Beach Shores?
faq.a: Costs depend on your course provider and the state's current fee schedule, and both change over time. Expect charges for the course, fingerprinting, the DBPR application, and the exam fee; confirm current totals with the Florida DBPR.

faq.q: Can I work as an agent in Daytona Beach Shores without a broker?
faq.a: No. A Florida sales associate license must be activated by a licensed broker before you can work with clients. Your license stays inactive until that happens, in Daytona Beach Shores or anywhere else in the state.

faq.q: How long does licensing take for Daytona Beach Shores candidates?
faq.a: Most people finish in two to four months, from enrolling in the 63-hour course through fingerprinting, the DBPR application, the state exam, and activating with a broker.
